claim: Nanodiscs are membrane mimetics that consist of a protein belt surrounding a lipid bilayer.
source: Nanodiscs are membrane mimetics that consist of a protein belt surrounding a lipid bilayer, and are broadly used for characterization of membrane proteins.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about nanodiscs found in the abstract, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: Nanodiscs are broadly used for characterization of membrane proteins.
source: Nanodiscs are membrane mimetics that consist of a protein belt surrounding a lipid bilayer, and are broadly used for characterization of membrane proteins.
evidence: This statement reflects established practice in the field, supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: The ΔH5-DMPC and ΔH4H5-DMPC nanodiscs display conformational heterogeneity with various elliptical shapes.
source: We find that it displays conformational heterogeneity with various elliptical shapes, and with substantial differences in lipid ordering in the centre and rim of the discs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by SAXS/SANS data, MD simulations, and integrative analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: There are substantial differences in lipid ordering in the centre and rim of the nanodiscs.
source: We find that it displays conformational heterogeneity with various elliptical shapes, and with substantial differences in lipid ordering in the centre and rim of the discs.
evidence: This finding is supported by MD simulation analysis of lipid order parameters shown in Figure 4.

claim: Nanodiscs are derived from and very similar to the human ApoA1 protein from high density lipoproteins (HDL particles).
source: They are derived from, and very similar to, the human ApoA1 protein from high density lipoproteins (HDL particles) and consist of two amphipatic membrane scaffold proteins (MSPs) that stack and encircle a small patch of lipids in a membrane bilayer to form a discoidal assembly.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the origin and design of nanodiscs.

claim: Nanodiscs consist of two amphipathic membrane scaffold proteins (MSPs) that stack and encircle a small patch of lipids in a membrane bilayer to form a discoidal assembly.
source: They are derived from, and very similar to, the human ApoA1 protein from high density lipoproteins (HDL particles) and consist of two amphipatic membrane scaffold proteins (MSPs) that stack and encircle a small patch of lipids in a membrane bilayer to form a discoidal assembly.
evidence: This is a structural description of nanodiscs based on established knowledge.

claim: Nanodisc diameters can be controlled and can range from about 7 to 13 nm.
source: The popularity of nanodiscs arises from their ability to mimic a membrane while at the same time ensuring a small system of homogeneous composition, the size of which can be controlled and can give diameters in a range from about 7 to 13 nm (Denisov et al., 2004; Hagn et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Mass spectrometry experiments have provided insight into lipid-water interactions and heterogeneous lipid compositions in nanodiscs.
source: For example, mass spectrometry experiments have provided insight into lipid-water interactions and heterogeneous lipid compositions (Marty et al., 2014; Marty et al., 2015), solid state NMR has been used to quantify lipid phase transition states and lipid order (Mörs et al., 2013; Martinez et al., 2017) and small angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) and -neutron scattering (SANS) have provided insight into the size and low resolution shape of nanodiscs in solution (Denisov et al., 2004; Skar-Gislinge et al., 2010; Midtgaard et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous mass spectrometry studies.

claim: Solid state NMR has been used to quantify lipid phase transition states and lipid order in nanodiscs.
source: For example, mass spectrometry experiments have provided insight into lipid-water interactions and heterogeneous lipid compositions (Marty et al., 2014; Marty et al., 2015), solid state NMR has been used to quantify lipid phase transition states and lipid order (Mörs et al., 2013; Martinez et al., 2017) and small angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) and -neutron scattering (SANS) have provided insight into the size and low resolution shape of nanodiscs in solution (Denisov et al., 2004; Skar-Gislinge et al., 2010; Midtgaard et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous NMR studies.

claim: SAXS and SANS have provided insight into the size and low resolution shape of nanodiscs in solution.
source: For example, mass spectrometry experiments have provided insight into lipid-water interactions and heterogeneous lipid compositions (Marty et al., 2014; Marty et al., 2015), solid state NMR has been used to quantify lipid phase transition states and lipid order (Mörs et al., 2013; Martinez et al., 2017) and small angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) and -neutron scattering (SANS) have provided insight into the size and low resolution shape of nanodiscs in solution (Denisov et al., 2004; Skar-Gislinge et al., 2010; Midtgaard et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous SAXS/SANS studies.

claim: MD simulations have provided pioneering insights into the structure of nanodiscs.
source: These experiments have been complemented by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations that provided both pioneering insights into the structure (Shih et al., 2005; Shih et al., 2007) as well as a better understanding of the assembly process, lipid-protein interactions and how much a nanodisc mimicks the membrane bilayer (Siuda and Tieleman, 2015; Debnath and Schäfer, 2015; Vestergaard et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous MD simulation studies.

claim: MD simulations have provided understanding of the assembly process, lipid-protein interactions and how much a nanodisc mimics the membrane bilayer.
source: These experiments have been complemented by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations that provided both pioneering insights into the structure (Shih et al., 2005; Shih et al., 2007) as well as a better understanding of the assembly process, lipid-protein interactions and how much a nanodisc mimicks the membrane bilayer (Siuda and Tieleman, 2015; Debnath and Schäfer, 2015; Vestergaard et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous MD simulation studies.

claim: A high resolution structure of the MSP protein belt encircling the nanodisc was recently obtained from the small, helix-5-deleted nanodisc, MSP1D1ΔH5 (ΔH5), reconstituted with DMPC lipids.
source: A high resolution structure of the MSP protein belt encircling the nanodisc was recently obtained from the small, helix-5-deleted nanodisc, MSP1D1ΔH5 (henceforth ΔH5), reconstituted with DMPC lipids (ΔH5-DMPC) (Bibow et al., 2017) by combining nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (Bibow et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the Bibow et al. 2017 study.

claim: The high resolution structure of ΔH5-DMPC was obtained by combining NMR spectroscopy, EPR spectroscopy and TEM.
source: A high resolution structure of the MSP protein belt encircling the nanodisc was recently obtained from the small, helix-5-deleted nanodisc, MSP1D1ΔH5 (henceforth ΔH5), reconstituted with DMPC lipids (ΔH5-DMPC) (Bibow et al., 2017) by combining nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (Bibow et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the Bibow et al. 2017 study.

claim: The NMR/EPR-derived structure of the belt proteins corresponded to an almost circularly-shaped disc.
source: Intriguingly, the resulting structure of the belt proteins corresponded to that of an almost circularly-shaped disc, while our previous SAXS/SANS investigations are clearly consistent with discs with an on-average elliptical cross-section (Skar-Gislinge et al., 2010; Midtgaard et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is based on the structure from Bibow et al. 2017, cited in the text.

claim: Previous SAXS/SANS investigations are clearly consistent with discs with an on-average elliptical cross-section.
source: Intriguingly, the resulting structure of the belt proteins corresponded to that of an almost circularly-shaped disc, while our previous SAXS/SANS investigations are clearly consistent with discs with an on-average elliptical cross-section (Skar-Gislinge et al., 2010; Midtgaard et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous SAXS/SANS studies by the authors.

claim: Optimal reconstitution ratios between DMPC lipids and ΔH5 and ΔH4H5 protein belts were determined based on SEC analysis.
source: We determined optimal reconstitution ratios between the DMPC lipids and the ΔH5 and ΔH4H5 protein belts to form lipid-saturated nanodiscs based on a size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a methodological claim supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Reconstitution ratios of 1:33 for ΔH4H5:DMPC and 1:50 for ΔH5:DMPC were optimal to form single and relatively narrow symmetric peaks.
source: In line with previous studies (Hagn et al., 2013), we found that reconstitution ratios of 1:33 for ΔH4H5:DMPC and 1:50 for ΔH5:DMPC were optimal in order to form single and relatively narrow symmetric peaks.
evidence: This claim is supported by SEC data and is consistent with previous studies cited.

claim: SAXS and SANS data exhibit a flat Guinier region at low q and indicate no signs of aggregation.
source: Our SAXS and SANS data all exhibit a flat Guinier region at low q and indicate no signs of aggregation (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the SAXS and SANS data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: In both ΔH5-DMPC and ΔH4H5-DMPC systems, the SAXS data exhibit an oscillation at medium to high q ([0.05:0.2] Å-1) arising from the combination of a negative excess scattering length density of the hydrophobic alkyl-chain bilayer core and positive excess scattering length densities of the hydrophilic lipid PC-headgroups and the amphipathic protein belt.
source: In both the ΔH5-DMPC and ΔH4H5-DMPC systems, the SAXS data exhibit an oscillation at medium to high q ([0.05:0.2] Å-1) arising from the combination of a negative excess scattering length density of the hydrophobic alkyl-chain bilayer core and positive excess scattering length densities of the hydrophilic lipid PC-headgroups and the amphipathic protein belt.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the SAXS data based on scattering theory and the known structure of nanodiscs.

claim: The SANS data decreases monotonically as a function of q in accordance with the homogeneous contrast situation present.
source: The SANS data decreases monotonically as a function of q in accordance with the homogeneous contrast situation present here.
evidence: This is an observation from the SANS data with interpretation based on scattering theory.

claim: The ΔH5-DMPC nanodiscs are slightly larger than the ΔH4H5-DMPC nanodiscs.
source: These two different contrast situations, core-shell-contrast for SAXS and bulk-contrast for SANS, are also clearly reflected in the obtained p(r)-functions (Figure 1C,D), which also confirm that the ΔH5-DMPC nanodiscs are slightly larger than the ΔH4H5-DMPC nanodiscs.
evidence: This claim is supported by the p(r)-functions shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: There are 65 ± 13 DMPC molecules in ΔH4H5 nanodiscs.
source: We find 65 ± 13 and 100 ± 14 DMPC molecules in the nanodiscs for ΔH4H5 and ΔH5, respectively, in agreement with the reconstitution ratios reported above.
evidence: This is a result from model fitting to SAXS/SANS data.

claim: There are 100 ± 14 DMPC molecules in ΔH5 nanodiscs.
source: We find 65 ± 13 and 100 ± 14 DMPC molecules in the nanodiscs for ΔH4H5 and ΔH5, respectively, in agreement with the reconstitution ratios reported above.
evidence: This is a result from model fitting to SAXS/SANS data.

claim: The effect of the DMPC melting transition is clearly reflected in the SAXS data where both the position of the first minimum and the shape of the oscillation changes as the DMPC transitions from the gel to the molten state.
source: The effect of the DMPC melting transition is clearly reflected in the SAXS data (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) where both the position of the first minimum and the shape of the oscillation changes as the DMPC transitions from the gel to the molten state.
evidence: This observation is supported by SAXS data at different temperatures shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The intensity of the forward scattering decreases significantly with increasing temperature.
source: We observe that the intensity of the forward scattering decreases significantly with increasing temperature, a result of the small but significant temperature-dependent change of the partial specific molecular volume of the DMPC.
evidence: This is an observation from SAXS data with interpretation based on physical properties of DMPC.

claim: The DMPC area per headgroup increases significantly as a result of the melting transition.
source: Here, the effect of the DMPC melting transition can clearly be seen on the obtained DMPC area per headgroup which increases significantly as a result of the melting.
evidence: This is a result from model fitting to SAXS data at different temperatures.

claim: An axis ratio of the formed discs different from unity (between 1.2 and 1.4) was found in all cases (with/without His-tag and below and above the DMPC melting temperature).
source: In all cases, that is, with/without His-tag and below and above the DMPC melting temperature, we found an axis ratio of the formed discs different from unity (between 1.2 and 1.4).
evidence: This is a result from model fitting to SAXS data under various conditions, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Neither the variation of temperature nor the removal of the His-tag affects the overall conclusion that elliptically-shaped nanodiscs describe the obtained small-angle scattering data.
source: Hence neither the variation of temperature nor the removal of the His-tag affects the overall conclusion that the elliptically-shaped nanodiscs describe the obtained small-angle scattering data.
evidence: This conclusion is based on analysis of SAXS data under different conditions.

claim: MD simulations were performed using the CHARMM36m force field.
source: We performed two simulations (total simulation time of 1196 ns) using the CHARMM36m force field (Huang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a methodological statement about the simulations performed.

claim: The three most populated clusters from MD simulations represent 95% of the simulations.
source: We visualized the conformational ensemble of the ΔH5-DMPC nanodisc by clustering the simulations, and found that the three most populated clusters represent 95% of the simulations.
evidence: This is a result from clustering analysis of the MD simulations.

claim: The three most populated clusters all have elliptical shapes, but differ in the directions of the major axis.
source: Notably, these structures all have elliptical shapes, but differ in the directions of the major axis (Figure 2A).
evidence: This observation is supported by visualization of the clusters shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The back-calculated SAXS from the NMR/EPR structure overshoots the depth of the SAXS minimum but captures well the shoulder observed in the experimental data.
source: When we use this structure to calculate the SAXS data, the back-calculated data overshoots the depth of the SAXS minimum but captures well the shoulder observed in the experimental data (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a comparison between SAXS calculated from the NMR/EPR structure and experimental SAXS data, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Neither the MD trajectory nor the NMR/EPR structure fit perfectly with the measured SAXS data.
source: Thus, neither the MD trajectory nor the NMR/EPR structure fit perfectly with the measured SAXS data.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparison of calculated and experimental SAXS data.

claim: The simulations show overall good agreement with NMR-derived distances between methyl groups.
source: When comparing the simulations to the NMR-derived distances between methyl groups (Figure 2C), we generally find good agreement, but observe a few distances that exceed the experimental upper bounds.
evidence: This is a comparison between distances calculated from simulations and experimental NOE data, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A few distances calculated from simulations exceed the experimental upper bounds for methyl NOEs.
source: When comparing the simulations to the NMR-derived distances between methyl groups (Figure 2C), we generally find good agreement, but observe a few distances that exceed the experimental upper bounds.
evidence: This is a comparison between distances calculated from simulations and experimental NOE data.

claim: The good agreement with amide NOEs mostly reflects that the secondary structures are maintained during the simulations.
source: As the amide NOEs are mostly sensitive to the local helical structure, the good agreement with this data mostly reflects that the secondary structures are maintained during the simulations.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the comparison between simulations and amide NOE data.

claim: The BME method refines the simulation against measured experimental averages by balancing minimizing the discrepancy between simulation and experiments and ensuring minimal perturbation of the original simulation.
source: Briefly, the BME method refines the simulation against measured experimental averages by balancing (1) minimizing the discrepancy between the simulation and the observed experimental averages and (2) ensuring as little perturbation of the original simulation as possible thereby limiting chances of overfitting.
evidence: This is a description of the BME method used in the study.

claim: Refining against SAXS data only improves the MD trajectory with respect to SAXS but not NOE data.
source: We find that refining against a single of the two data types only improves the MD trajectory with respect to the structural properties it is sensitive to, highlighting the orthogonal information in the two sources of information.
evidence: This is a result from BME reweighting analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: Clusters 1 and 2 together constitute about 80% of the conformational ensemble both before and after reweighting.
source: Clusters 1 and 2, which together constitute about 80% of the conformational ensemble (both before and after reweighting), are both clusters with high acylindricity, but with almost orthogonal directions of the major axis in the elliptical structure.
evidence: This is a result from cluster analysis of the ensemble.

claim: Clusters 1 and 2 are both clusters with high acylindricity, but with almost orthogonal directions of the major axis in the elliptical structure.
source: Clusters 1 and 2, which together constitute about 80% of the conformational ensemble (both before and after reweighting), are both clusters with high acylindricity, but with almost orthogonal directions of the major axis in the elliptical structure.
evidence: This is a result from cluster analysis of the ensemble.

claim: The major change after integration is the exchange in populations of clusters 1 and 2, resulting in cluster 2 being weighted highest.
source: The major change after integration is the exchange in populations of the two clusters resulting in cluster 2 to be weighted highest, underlining the influence and importance of the integration.
evidence: This is a result from BME reweighting analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The DMPC lipid bilayer in the ΔH5 nanodiscs is thinner and un-ordered near the protein belt and thicker and more ordered in the core of the nanodisc.
source: The results illustrates that the DMPC lipid bilayer in the ΔH5 nanodiscs is not homogeneous but rather thinner and un-ordered near the protein belt and thicker and more ordered in the core of the nanodisc, which in turn is more similar to a pure bilayer (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a result from analysis of lipid properties in the reweighted ensemble, shown in Figure 4.

claim: The core of the ΔH5 nanodisc is more similar to a pure bilayer than the rim.
source: The results illustrates that the DMPC lipid bilayer in the ΔH5 nanodiscs is not homogeneous but rather thinner and un-ordered near the protein belt and thicker and more ordered in the core of the nanodisc, which in turn is more similar to a pure bilayer (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a result from analysis of lipid properties in the reweighted ensemble, shown in Figure 4.

claim: The melting transition peak broadens significantly in all three nanodisc systems (ΔH4H5, ΔH5, MSP1D1) compared to that of pure DMPC vesicles.
source: In line with earlier DSC experiments (Shaw et al., 2004), our results show that the melting transition peak broadens significantly in all three nanodisc systems compared to that of pure DMPC vesicles (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a result from DSC experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: The transition enthalpy per mole of DMPC increases with the nanodisc size.
source: Our results show that the transition enthalpy per mole of DMPC, i.e. the area under the curves, increases with the nanodisc size, in line with previous observations for, respectively, DMPC and DPPC in MSP1D1 and in the larger MSP1E3D1 systems (Denisov et al., 2005), where it was proposed to be due to the absence of a cooperative melting transition of the lipids at the nanodisc rim (Denisov et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a result from DSC experiments, consistent with previous observations cited.

claim: In the smallest ΔH4H5 nanodisc, the DMPC has a TM ≈ 22.5°C.
source: In the smallest ΔH4H5 nanodisc, the DMPC has a TM ≈ 22.5°C.
evidence: This is a result from DSC experiments.

claim: In ΔH5 the DMPC has TM at 24.5°C which is close to that of the DMPC vesicles.
source: In ΔH5 the DMPC has TM at 24.5°C which is close to that of the DMPC vesicles, while the larger MSP1D1 nanodisc has a TM ≈ 28°C.
evidence: This is a result from DSC experiments.

claim: The larger MSP1D1 nanodisc has a TM ≈ 28°C.
source: In ΔH5 the DMPC has TM at 24.5°C which is close to that of the DMPC vesicles, while the larger MSP1D1 nanodisc has a TM ≈ 28°C.
evidence: This is a result from DSC experiments.

claim: The TM value of 28°C for DMPC in MSP1D1 is similar to the value of 28.5°C measured for DMPC melting in MSP1D1 by Denisov et al., 2005.
source: This TM value is similar to the value of 28.5°C measured for DMPC melting in MSP1D1 by Denisov et al., 2005, who in addition measured a TM value of 27.5°C in the even larger MSP1E3D1 discs.
evidence: This is a comparison to literature values from Denisov et al., 2005.

claim: DMPC-MSP interactions can both destabilize DMPC in the gel-phase in the smaller nanodiscs (ΔH4H5-DMPC) and stabilize the DMPC gel-phase in larger nanodiscs (MSP1D1-DMPC and MSP1E3D1-DMPC).
source: Our results point towards a non-trivial effect of the DMPC-MSP interactions. They can both destabilize DMPC in the gel-phase in the smaller nanodiscs (ΔH4H5-DMPC) where the low area-to-rim ratio leads to the lower TM compared to the DMPC vesicles, but also stabilize the DMPC gel-phase in larger nanodiscs with larger area-to-rim ratios such as MSP1D1-DMPC and MSP1E3D1-DMPC.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DSC results in the context of nanodisc size.

claim: The study reconciles previous apparently conflicting observations about the shape of nanodiscs.
source: Together, our results reconcile previous apparently conflicting observations about the shape of nanodiscs, and pave the way for future integrative studies of larger complex systems such as membrane proteins embedded in nanodiscs.
evidence: This is a summary claim about the overall contribution of the study.

claim: The study paves the way for future integrative studies of larger complex systems such as membrane proteins embedded in nanodiscs.
source: Together, our results reconcile previous apparently conflicting observations about the shape of nanodiscs, and pave the way for future integrative studies of larger complex systems such as membrane proteins embedded in nanodiscs.
evidence: This is a forward-looking statement about the implications of the study.

claim: The nanodisc possesses underlying elliptical fluctuations with the major axis changing within the nanodisc.
source: Combining the results of the two studies, we hypothesized that the nanodisc possesses underlying elliptical fluctuations with the major axis changing within the nanodisc.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that was tested and supported by the integrative analysis.

claim: NMR and EPR measurements, which build on ensemble averaged information of specific atom-atom interactions, will give rise to an on-average circular structure in a system with elliptical fluctuations where the major axis changes direction.
source: In such a system NMR and EPR measurements, which build on ensemble averaged information of specific atom-atom interactions, will give rise to an on-average circular structure.
evidence: This is an inference about how NMR/EPR data would appear for a dynamically elliptical system.

claim: SAXS and SANS, which build on distributions of global distances rather than specific atom-atom distances, will not distinguish between the orientation of the major axis within the nanodisc and thus give rise to observations of an elliptical shape.
source: SAXS and SANS, on the contrary, which build on distributions of global distances rather than specific atom-atom distances, will not distinguish between the orientation of the major axis within the nanodisc and thus give rise to observations of an elliptical shape.
evidence: This is an inference about how SAXS/SANS data would appear for a dynamically elliptical system.

claim: The MD simulations and integration with experiments support the hypothesis of underlying elliptical fluctuations with the major axis changing direction inside the nanodisc.
source: Thus, our MD simulations and the integration with the experiments support the hypothesis of underlying elliptical fluctuations with the major axis changing direction inside the nanodisc, and we note that the detailed molecular description of this was only possible by combining the MD simulations with both the SAXS and NMR data.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the integrative analysis of MD simulations with SAXS and NMR data.

claim: The detailed molecular description of the elliptical fluctuations was only possible by combining the MD simulations with both the SAXS and NMR data.
source: Thus, our MD simulations and the integration with the experiments support the hypothesis of underlying elliptical fluctuations with the major axis changing direction inside the nanodisc, and we note that the detailed molecular description of this was only possible by combining the MD simulations with both the SAXS and NMR data.
evidence: This is a statement about the necessity of the integrative approach.

claim: The results are in line with previous simulation studies on larger DMPC nanodiscs (MSP1, MSP1E1 and MSP1E2).
source: These results are in line with previous simulation studies on the larger DMPC nanodiscs, MSP1, MSP1E1 and MSP1E2 (Siuda and Tieleman, 2015; Debnath and Schäfer, 2015), albeit performed without experimental reweighting, as well as with solid state NMR data on the both ΔH5-DMPC and the larger MSP1-DMPC (Mörs et al., 2013; Martinez et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous simulation studies cited.

claim: The results are in line with solid state NMR data on both ΔH5-DMPC and the larger MSP1-DMPC.
source: These results are in line with previous simulation studies on the larger DMPC nanodiscs, MSP1, MSP1E1 and MSP1E2 (Siuda and Tieleman, 2015; Debnath and Schäfer, 2015), albeit performed without experimental reweighting, as well as with solid state NMR data on the both ΔH5-DMPC and the larger MSP1-DMPC (Mörs et al., 2013; Martinez et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous NMR studies cited.

claim: The broader melting transition in nanodiscs is in line with the observed differentiated lipid ordering from the reweighted simulations.
source: The broader melting transition is in line with the observed differentiated lipid ordering in nanodiscs from the reweighted simulations, as the observed differences in how ordered the lipids are necessarily will cause differences in the melting temperature and thus give rise to the broader peaks.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting DSC results to simulation results.

claim: The broadened peaks in DSC are in line with results observed in previous solid state NMR experiments which found a substantially broadened and diminished lipid gel-liquid phase transition in the ΔH5-DMPC nanodisc in the temperature range 10-28°C.
source: Furthermore, the broadened peaks are in line with results observed in previous solid state NMR experiments which found a substantially broadened and diminished lipid gel-liquid phase transition in the ΔH5-DMPC nanodisc in the temperature range 10-28°C (Martinez et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous NMR results cited.

claim: The belt proteins induce additional disorder to the lipid tails near the rim.
source: In particular, our results suggest that the belt proteins induces additional disorder to the lipid tails near the rim.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the lipid order parameter results from simulations.
